summary: The Pentagon continued its document release pace this week, publishing its sixth batch of UAP files on September 18th alongside newly digitized audio from a 1952 Project Blue Book briefing, while also launching a fresh disclosure pathway for government insiders to report UAP information with updated waivers. Meanwhile, the White House sidestepped direct questions about whether the U.S. military shot down unidentified objects in recent years, leaving that claim essentially unresolved. Journalist Ross Coulthart challenged the effectiveness of the new whistleblower protections, calling them insufficient for true transparency, while astrophysicist Matthew Szydagis and Harvard researcher Avi Loeb continued examining the physical characteristics of reported UAP sightings. Congressional sentiment shifted noticeably as lawmakers acknowledged that UAP sightings themselves haven't changed over decades, but public willingness to discuss them has finally broken through the stigma.
